45267c85e7:
The summer program, which lasts two to three weeks, is run in partnership with the Hebrew University and gives participants a comprehensive picture of the latest developments in the field of trauma in general, and in the Israeli context in particular. The course includes theoretical lectures, experiential learning and educational field trips.

Students learn about risk factors for developing post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), symptoms of associated distress, and potential protective factors. The course presents theories and research on the effects of trauma, healthy coping processes and possible pathological consequences. Guiding principles for treating post-traumatic disorders are also discussed.

The field trips and lectures include meetings with researchers and professionals in the field of trauma.

## Optional follow-up week: clinical training in cognitive behavioral therapy for post-traumatic disorders

In addition to the course, an optional third week of clinical training is offered for therapists who want to specialize in trauma therapy (40 academic hours, 2 credits). This training is based on the three-phase model of trauma treatment. The first phase, stabilization, focuses on self-regulation techniques. The second phase, trauma processing, includes exposure techniques and building a narrative. The third phase, integration, calls for cognitive techniques. During the training week, students will review the literature in the field, discuss the treatment model, watch demonstrations of the techniques and practice them with one another by working with their own personal experiences.

**Please note: the course is taught in English. The third week is for therapists only.**

## Background on the PANDA program

The PANDA program - "Here We Learn Ways of Coping" - helps children and parents develop their emotion regulation abilities and ways of coping. The program is run in a group, is designed for children aged 7-12, and includes 8 sessions for children and 3 sessions for parents. The program combines mindfulness techniques, cognitive-behavioral techniques and narrative interventions, all woven into the program in a creative and enjoyable way.

What sets PANDA apart from similar programs is that it is designed for every child, not only for children who show worrying behaviors or are experiencing significant difficulty. The program's basic premise is that everyone can benefit from emotion regulation tools, and that these tools will stay with them throughout their lives.

The PANDA program was developed by Prof. Ruth Pat-Horenczyk and Sarit Schramm-Yavin at "Metiv - The Israel Psychotrauma Center".

The course is for mental health therapists who work with parents and parenting and want to expand their professional toolbox and run PANDA for Parents groups.

The course includes three sessions of four academic hours each, for a total of 12 academic hours. The curriculum covers content on trauma, emotion regulation and parenting, an introduction to DBT skills, and practice of mindfulness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance and interpersonal skills. The course will also discuss the process of building a group, recruiting participants and evaluating the program.

## Background on the PANDA for Parents program

PANDA for Parents groups were developed by Sarit Schramm-Yavin and Tzipora Hayat as a follow-on to the PANDA program ("Here We Learn Ways of Coping") for ages 7-12, out of the understanding that parenting can challenge our ability to cope with stress and can intensify mood swings. By its very nature, parenting confronts parents with frustration, uncertainty, helplessness and even despair. The program aims to teach practical emotion regulation tools that can help in coping with challenging parenting situations. The program is based on the dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) approach, which includes practical tools for regulating emotions, coping with stressful situations and managing relationships with others, and includes exercises from the PANDA for Children program.

## Background on the PANDA for Two program

The PANDA for Two program is a reworking of the "Let's Make Room for Play" (NAMAL) program, developed by Prof. Esther Cohen and Prof. Ruth Pat-Horenczyk for Metiv. It is a model of play-focused group work for pairs of parents and young children, aimed at developing parents' playfulness and capacity for abstraction so that they can promote and support the development of regulation abilities in their children.

The program is designed for parent-toddler pairs aged 2-3 who are dealing with difficulties typical of this age and/or are exposed to stress, crisis or trauma. The program includes 6 parent-and-child sessions for about 8 dyads. Each session has a psychoeducational message aimed at parents and expressed in a short, catchy saying. The messages are conveyed through shared play, music, drama and movement activities suited to ages 2-3.

## The program's key messages

- **The parent-child bond** as a protective, secure base
- **Encouraging independence and self-confidence**
- **Playfulness**, humor and creativity
- **Reflecting** actions and intentions
- **Expressing and reflecting emotions**
